_README: T282 HAND ADJUDICATION of every citation the checker flagged that the
keyword adjudicator in population-table.py could not decide.
Keyed 'file:line:cited-id'. Every entry carries its REASON: a verdict with
no reason is not a verdict. Decided by reading the recorded gloss against
BOTH rules' text in patterns.md at the sha named in the T282 handoff.
Data, not prose, so the handoff table RENDERS from this rather than
restating it -- P-80: never restate a corrected value; make the second

.softhouse/conformance.sh:1832:70: P-70 IS '"not found" is a statement about the search'. Correctly cited. The gloss ran on into a following sentence about the fail-open linter's CORPUS, and that is what scored P-76.

.softhouse/handoff/2026-08-17-run1-harne: The same measurement-report line as SWEEP.txt:504, quoted into the handoff. Same adjudication.
.softhouse/capture/t91/PREDICTION.md:67:: The gloss is a procedural aside about commit ancestry ('the prediction commit is a parent of the evidence commit'), and restates neither P-9 nor P-17.
.softhouse/handoff/2026-08-17-run1-harne: ADJACENT PAIR, not adjudicable from the text alone. P-11 = 'the code can be RIGHT and its stated reason WRONG'. P-12 = 'a right conclusion on a wrong reason RECURS IN THE ARTEFACT written to record it'. The gloss 'conclusion, wrong reason, PROPAGATED INTO A DURABLE FILE' leans P-12, but P-11 is P-12's own premise. Left for the author rather than guessed.
.softhouse/handoff/2026-08-21-run2-tierA: RELATED PAIR. P-58 = 'when N attempts disagree about a tool, COUNT THE PROGRAMS before you count the votes'. P-75 = 'grep and rg in an agent shell are not the programs you think'. The gloss states the host FACT (P-75) inside an argument for the METHOD (P-58). Both defensible.

P-71 IS 'a worker's fork point is UNPREDICTABLE: MEASURE IT, NEVER ASSERT IT', and the gloss is 'the fork point, MEASURED, not assumed'. Exactly right. P-24 ('an assertion about what happens ON MERGE can only be tested BY MERGING') won on the shared token alone.
The 'gloss' is a MARKDOWN HEADING about a guard handling exit codes correctly, which is P-81's own subject. Correctly cited; P-93 won on 'guard'.
